tagline: West to the Red Banks, where Handy played a barbecue.
intro: From the Owensboro bypass, US 60 runs west through Stanley and over the Green River at Spottsville to Henderson on the Ohio, then on through Corydon, Waverly and Morganfield, where KY 56 turns south to the Webster County line.

W. C. Handy, who called himself the Father of the Blues, spent about a decade in Henderson. Playing a barbecue there in 1896, he met Elizabeth Price, and they were married that July. The town had begun as Red Banks, for the reddish clay of its bluffs, and shortly before World War I it was said to have more millionaires per head than any city in the world. Then Britain put a high tariff on imported tobacco.

moments.title: Spottsville
moments.text: From the US 60 bridge over the Green River you can see the lock, and a railroad bridge that turns aside whenever a barge comes through.

moments.title: Henderson
moments.text: John James Audubon kept a store here in the 1810s before he turned to art full time, and the state park named for him holds the largest collection of his memorabilia anywhere.

moments.title: Corydon
moments.text: Patsy Dorsey named the town for the hero of a song called "Pastoral Elegy", who had taken his own name from a lovesick shepherd in Virgil.

sources.label: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways
